subject: Immunology
vignette: A 3-week-old boy is brought to the emergency department after a generalized tonic-clonic seizure. He has a heart murmur and mild facial dysmorphism. Serum calcium is 6.0 mg/dL with an inappropriately low parathyroid hormone level, and chest radiography shows a narrow superior mediastinum with no visible thymic shadow. Echocardiography demonstrates truncus arteriosus, and a 22q11.2 deletion is later confirmed.
question: This patient's findings are best explained by abnormal development of which of the following?

options.text: The first and second pharyngeal arches
The second pharyngeal pouch and aortic sac
The third and fourth pharyngeal pouches, with their neural crest contributions
The sixth pharyngeal pouch and the thyroid diverticulum

explanation_correct: DiGeorge syndrome results from failure of the third and fourth pharyngeal pouches and their neural crest contributions, which give rise to the thymus and the inferior parathyroids (third pouch) and the superior parathyroids (fourth pouch). The neural crest also forms the conotruncal septum, so affected infants present with hypocalcemic seizures from hypoparathyroidism, a conotruncal cardiac defect such as truncus arteriosus or tetralogy of Fallot, and T cell deficiency from thymic hypoplasia. The presentation is captured by the mnemonic CATCH-22: Cardiac defect, Abnormal facies, Thymic hypoplasia, Cleft palate, Hypocalcemia, and chromosome 22q11 deletion.

explanation_incorrect.A: First and second arch defects produce mandibulofacial and conductive hearing abnormalities, not thymic and parathyroid aplasia.
explanation_incorrect.B: An isolated fourth aortic arch abnormality explains vascular rings, not the combination of T cell deficiency and hypocalcemia.
explanation_incorrect.C: The second pouch gives rise to the palatine tonsil and the third pharyngeal pouch, not the thymus and parathyroids.
explanation_incorrect.E: The thyroid derives from a floor-of-pharynx diverticulum and is unrelated to the thymic and parathyroid aplasia seen here.

educationalObjective: DiGeorge syndrome reflects failed third and fourth pharyngeal pouch development, causing thymic and parathyroid aplasia with conotruncal cardiac defects.

subject: Immunology
vignette: A 33-year-old asymptomatic woman has an incidental 4-cm mediastinal mass on chest computed tomography performed for unrelated reasons. Excisional biopsy shows a single enlarged lymph node with small, regressed germinal centers surrounded by concentric rings of mantle-zone lymphocytes, penetrating hyalinized blood vessels, and prominent follicular dendritic cell networks. She has no systemic symptoms and no laboratory abnormalities.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Hyaline-vascular Castleman disease is a localized lymphoid hyperplasia that typically presents as a solitary, asymptomatic mediastinal mass. Histologically it shows regressed germinal centers with concentric 'onion skin' mantle zones, penetrating hyalinized vessels ('lollipop' lesions), and expanded follicular dendritic cell meshworks. It is important because it mimics lymphoma clinically but is benign and usually cured by excision; the multicentric plasma cell variant instead causes systemic inflammatory symptoms and is associated with HHV-8.

explanation_incorrect.A: Follicular lymphoma shows back-to-back follicles with BCL2-positive germinal center cells and t(14;18), not onion-skin mantles with penetrating vessels.
explanation_incorrect.C: Reactive follicular hyperplasia produces enlarged, active germinal centers with tingible body macrophages rather than regressed centers and hyalinized vessels.
explanation_incorrect.D: Nodular sclerosis Hodgkin lymphoma shows collagen bands and Reed-Sternberg cells, which are absent here.
explanation_incorrect.E: Tuberculous lymphadenitis produces caseating granulomas, not onion-skin mantle zones around regressed germinal centers.

educationalObjective: Hyaline-vascular Castleman disease is a benign lymphoid hyperplasia presenting as a solitary mass with onion-skin mantle zones and penetrating hyalinized vessels.
